title: StatusData
description:
`status`'s reply data.

```json
{"version": "0.10.3", "pid": 4242, "platform": "macos", "protocol_version": 1,
 "capabilities": [], "seq": 0, "clients": {"app": 0, "tui": 0, "remote": 0, "cli": 1},
 "gate": "signed app only", "brain": {"restarts": 0, "handled": 0},
 "claude": {"installed": true, "version": "2.1.314", "signed_in": true,
            "auth_method": "claude.ai", "account": "…", "plan": "pro"},
 "runs": {"live": 0, "queued": 0}, "jobs": {"count": 0},
 "paths": {"home": "…", "socket": "…", "lock": "…", "token": "…", "logs": "…"}}
```

`brain`, `runs` and `jobs` hold zeros until the brain, the runner and the scheduler
fill them, and `seq` is 0 until the event bus does.

capabilities.description:
What this rlxd can do, by name, as `hello`'s reply lists it. A client ignores names
it does not know.

claude.description: The Claude Code rlxd runs: `RLXD_CLAUDE_BIN`, or `claude` on `PATH`.

clients.description:
The connections open now, by the role their `hello` was let in as. A refused
`hello` is never counted.

dev_features.description:
The development-only cargo features this rlxd was built with, by name, such as
the one that lets it run in gate dev mode (5.1): a build for development and CI.
Absent from a release build, which has none.

gate.description:
Who may be the tool-call gate (5.1): `signed app only`, or `dev mode (unsigned
app accepted)` while rlxd runs in gate dev mode.

paths.description: Where this rlxd keeps what it serves and writes.

pid.description:
rlxd's process id, from 1 to 2147483647 (2^31 - 1), so a client's `kill` of it, a
C `int`, can never be `kill(-1)`.

pipe_acl.description:
Windows only: whom the named pipe's DACL admits. `current_user` says it holds one
entry, for the user rlxd runs as, which rlxd read back from the live pipe. Absent
on macOS and Linux, where the socket's mode, 0600, does that.

platform.description: The OS rlxd runs on: `macos`, `linux` or `windows`.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version of the connection that asked.

seq.description: The `seq` of the latest event on this home's event stream, or 0 before the first.

pid.description: Its process id, while one runs: from 1 to 2147483647 (2^31 - 1), as rlxd's.

restarts.description: How many times rlxd started it again.

Claude.description:
The Claude Code rlxd runs, and its sign-in, as `claude --version` and
`claude auth status --json` report them. rlxd reads no credential store itself.

account.description: The account it is signed in as: its email address.

auth_method.description: How it is signed in, such as `claude.ai`.

installed.description:
Whether rlxd found the program: `RLXD_CLAUDE_BIN` when it is set, else `claude`
on `PATH`.

plan.description: The account's plan, such as `pro` or `max`.

signed_in.description: Whether it is signed in. False when it is not installed, or would not say.

version.description: Its version, such as `2.1.314`, when `claude --version` said one.

Clients.description: The connections open now, by `hello` role.

app.description: rlxapp, the gate: connections whose `hello {role: "app"}` passed the gate checks.

cli.description: Command-line clients, such as `rlxd call` and `rlxd-hook`, the one asking included.

db.description:
The scheduler's database, `<home>/rlxd/rlxd.db`: `ok`, or `set_aside` when rlxd
found one it could not read (corrupt, or from a newer rlxd), moved it aside and
began a fresh one. Absent: `ok`.

set_aside.description: Where a database it could not read was moved, with why.

Paths.description: Where this rlxd keeps what it serves and writes, as it resolved them from the home.

lock.description: The lock file rlxd holds while it runs, one rlxd per home.

socket.description:
Where clients connect: the socket's path on macOS and Linux, the named pipe's
name on Windows.

token.description: The file holding the shared client token.
